question: Does the browser decode and preprocess every REAL capture format the way the reference decoder does?
lineage: QG-03b-2 — raised by QG-03b, which proved only the PNG path. JPEG is a real capture format; WebP is not.
scope: 45 fixture/encoding pairs (9 sources x 5 encodings) across 8 browser/backend/display cells. Compares the browser's decode of THE EXACT ENCODED BYTES against Pillow's decode of the same bytes, then the authoritative preprocessing contract on both. Does NOT reopen QG-03b's PNG result except as a regression check, does NOT reopen any QG-03 cell verdict, and does NOT adopt the detector.

workstation.os: Microsoft Windows 11 Home Single Language, build 26200 (10.0.26200)
workstation.note: TWO GPUs are present, so a WebGPU figure is only attributable if the adapter is identified. The harness records adapterInfo where the browser exposes it; Firefox exposes an empty adapterInfo (S-02), so every Firefox WebGPU figure here is labelled 'adapter unidentified'.

platform_coverage.linux: NOT MEASURED. Firefox on Linux remains UNKNOWN, exactly as S-02a-1 left it. Nothing in this experiment touches that cell and nothing here may be quoted about it.

chromium.why_not_branded_chrome: Chrome 152 stable REFUSES --load-extension and does so with a warning the harness never sees, so the extension is simply absent and the run looks like 'the capability is missing in extension contexts'. That false negative cost two runs during S-01.
chromium.extension_context: MV3 service worker drives a chrome.offscreen document; ORT runs in the offscreen document. ORT CANNOT run in an MV3 service worker at all — it loads its WASM glue by dynamic import(), which the HTML specification forbids there (S-03).

firefox.extension_context: MV3 event page — a document with a DOM, so ORT runs there directly and no offscreen equivalent is invented
firefox.prefs_forced_why: REPORTING ONLY. Firefox MV3 gates host_permissions behind user-granted origin controls (S-02a-2); without this the probe runs correctly but cannot deliver its report, which is indistinguishable from a crash.
firefox.prefs_not_forced_why: S-02a fixed the rule in advance: 'a result requiring an about:config change on the release channel is CONDITIONAL, never ACCEPT, because the judging machine will not have that change.' If the Firefox WebGPU cell fails at defaults, that failure IS the result.

runtime.bundle: ort.all.min.js (carries both wasm and webgpu backends)
runtime.loading: ADR-0001's own path — installVerifiedOrtRuntime() hashes the packaged ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.wasm against ORT_PIN before ORT is touched, then createPinnedInferenceSession() creates the session. The SHIPPED @pratibimb/security module is used, not a copy.
runtime.wasm_artifacts_why_not: 27.8 MB. CI blocks files over 5 MB and SECURITY.md requires large binaries be referenced by pinned revision. build-qg03-extension.mjs pulls them from the pinned npm package.

model_under_test.why_not_committed: .gitignore excludes artifacts/models/ and scripts/verify-repo.py bans .onnx. The TRACKED authority on which artifact the project has published evidence for is artifacts/gates/T1-detector-training/qg05-detector-evaluation.json, and the reference generator refuses to run if the local file disagrees with it.
model_under_test.delivery: inlined as base64 in the probe. The model performs ZERO fetches, so 'no runtime model download' is observable in the arrival log rather than asserted.
model_under_test.provenance: trained in this repository by tools/detector/train.py on the project's own synthetic rendered set. Nothing downloaded. Option B of constitution §8.
model_under_test.note: UNCHANGED. Used only to answer whether a format change moves what the detector says.

reference.rule: the reference decodes THE EXACT ENCODED BYTES whose sha256 is recorded and re-verified in the browser, then runs the authoritative preprocessing contract. A lossy format is never compared against the original lossless image - that would measure compression, not conformance.
reference.iccProfiles: never embedded - a browser applies colour management from one and Pillow does not
reference.encoderSettings: every knob explicit: JPEG subsampling, optimize and progressive pinned; WebP lossless/quality/method pinned

cases: 13 procedural fixtures - square, wide, tall, odd, tiny, upscale, asymmetric-padding - built from 1px rules, a Nyquist checkerboard and exact corner markers, because a smooth gradient is the image on which two kernels agree
2 real rendered dataset frames (dev-0000 960x640, dev-0003 1152x640) decoded from real PNGs by the browser itself

measurements.stages: decoded / letterboxed / tensor, by SHA-256 against the Python reference, plus max/mean/fraction where they differ
measurements.decodeVariants: three per fixture - default, colorSpaceConversion:'none' (isolates COLOUR MANAGEMENT), premultiplyAlpha:'none' (isolates the canvas ALPHA round trip) - so a divergence can be attributed rather than reported
measurements.detection: same encoded bytes -> browser decode -> preprocessing -> ORT -> shipped decode -> CSS boxes, against the QG-03 reference boxes
measurements.latency: decode and preprocess timed SEPARATELY, per format
measurements.referenceDumps: fetched from the extension's own origin rather than inlined - 45 decoded RGB images is ~124 MB

csp.directive: built by the SHIPPED buildExtensionPagesCsp(), so the harness cannot run under a policy the product would reject
csp.connect_src: pinned to the loopback collector — the harness's only legitimate destination
csp.status: ADR-0001 is UNCHANGED by this experiment.

data.real_user_data: none — the frames are synthetic rendered HTML from the project's own generator
data.profiles: temporary, deleted after each run; spawned Firefox processes reaped by PID-set difference and the reap verified

known_harness_defects_found_and_fixed: The probe originally treated a FRAME_NOT_OPAQUE refusal as a failure. Refusing an untrustworthy frame IS the conformant behaviour, so the probe now records it as such - otherwise the alpha fixture would have counted against three formats for doing the right thing.

Two pre-existing tests built synthetic RGBA buffers whose alpha channel was not 255. They were testing opaque preprocessing and did not know it; the new guard exposed them. Fixed to be explicitly opaque rather than by weakening the guard.

capture_formats.jpeg: REAL — captureVisibleTab({format:'jpeg', quality}). Measured at q95 and q62.
capture_formats.webp: NOT a capture format. captureVisibleTab cannot produce it and TabsCaptureApi declares png|jpeg. Every WebP reference in dossier v4.0 is the T2 EGRESS encoding - 'Encode WebP q62, then decode the bytes back' is the redaction verification pass. Measured anyway because CaptureFrame.format permits 'webp' while the adapter cannot produce one.
